text:
Vantry's maglev prototype hit 540 km/h on 14 March 2031, the highest speed recorded by the vehicle to date.

The run came during the final acceleration trial at the Orrin Flats test corridor. The prototype held 540 km/h for 38 seconds, covering a 21 km stretch of the 48 km guideway.

Dr. Selwyn Marachek, chief test engineer at the Vantry Transit Authority, oversaw the run and confirmed the reading.

The figure appears in Trial Report VTA-MX-17, which the Authority released after independent verification of both onboard and trackside speed logs.

**What it means for the sector:** Holding top speed for 38 seconds, rather than touching it briefly, is the number buyers and regulators will study. Sustained running on a 21 km stretch suggests the system can operate at the limit, not merely reach it. Independent log verification should also ease due diligence for prospective partners and investors.
